chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Slide trombone versus valve and the voice-like quarter tone
summary: The slide trombone can bend between positions like a voice or cello, and he says he never had a lesson and goes by instinct.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about the trombone. It's a different kind of instrument.
Well, there's two types of trombone. There's a valve and a slide. Which one are you speaking of?
Mostly the slide, because the valve always seemed to me to be just like a trumpet with a...

Well, I would think it is sort of that way. Unless you could... A lot of people can bend notes with their lips, you know; or either use half-valves and you can use the half-valve and bend the note. But with the trombone, with the slide trombone, you can go in between the position and get a note like you would call a jazz note. You know, like you would have a B-natural and C. Well, there's a quarter sound in between there that you can make
with the trombone that you can't do with the ordinary horn, unless you have a flexible...a very flexible lip. I mean, that you can do...that is, with a trumpet or any other valve instrument.

But with a slide, you see... The slide is more like a human voice. Like, your voice, you can bend it and make different noises. And the same thing goes with the slide. It's more akin to your voice. In other words, like a cello or a violin, you can...you've got an in-between sound you can make. You understand? I think you would call it a quarter-tone, but I'm not sure. So that's what I think. I mean, don't take my word as the prayer book! Because I never had a lesson, so I don't know. I just go by instinct and all of the makings of the horn...I mean, the mechanics of music... I do it my own self. And from things that I have heard from different people. I mean, I heard them and I kept them in mind. I try to keep an open mind.
Those people you're talking about, were they not necessarily trombone players but people who played other instruments?
Yeah, musicians. Musicians... I couldn't tell you just whom I heard it from. But I have heard it in different places and different things.
